section.p: The metR HTML to DITA converter does not rely on visual formatting alone. It reads structural information from HTML elements and semantic markup. When those elements are applied correctly, the converter and AI Agent can:

ul.li: Generate a root Ditamap and child Ditamaps from the index file, ZIP folder name, or document title.
Detect topic boundaries from heading levels and establish the Ditamap hierarchy.
Classify topic types: concept (descriptive), task (procedural), reference (tabular or lookup), or troubleshooting.
Convert paragraphs, lists, tables, images, links, inline formatting, and code blocks to valid DITA elements.
Infer metadata — short descriptions, keywords, index terms, author, and revision history — from <head> meta tags and structured body elements.
Flag issues such as missing short descriptions, invalid links, duplicate IDs, orphan topics, and improper nesting for human review.

section.p: The converter reads the following HTML constructs to accomplish this. Each is covered in a dedicated section of this guide:

row.entry: Index file title (index.html or index.htm)
Becomes the root Ditamap <title> element. If no index file exists, the ZIP folder name is used instead.
Heading 1
Drives the Ditamap hierarchy and primary topic boundaries.
Heading 2 – Heading N
Each heading generates a separate child Ditamap and a corresponding DITA topic, nested according to heading level.
Paragraphs

Maps to

elements inside topic body elements.
Tables
Converts to <simpletable> or to a CALS <table> + <tgroup>
Images and Graphics
Converts to DITA <image> elements with optional <alt> text. Block images are wrapped in <fig>.
Ordered lists
Maps to DITA <ol><li> or to <steps><step><cmd> structures.
Unordered lists
Maps to DITA <ul><li> elements or <prereq> in task topics.
Index file hierarchy
Used to build the root Ditamap navigation hierarchy; not converted as a regular DITA topic.
Metadata
Maps to Ditamap metadata and topic <prolog> elements including <author>, <critdates>, and <keywords>.
Character formatting (bold, italic, monospace)
Maps to bold <b>, italic <i>, or inline code <codeph> elements.
Admonitions (note, warning, tip, important, caution)
Maps to the DITA <note> element with the appropriate type attribute.
Cross - References and Hyperlinks
Maps to DITA cross-reference <xref> element with appropriate scope and format attributes.
Math and Equations
Maps to <equation-block> for block equations or inline <math> for inline equations, with MathML content preserved.
